data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) sets the United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) policy for system and information integrity (SII).
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) policy for system and information integrity (SII)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all:
Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and USDA personnel who work for or on behalf of USDA.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and USDA personnel who work for or on behalf of USDA
conditions: who work for or on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The term “USDA personnel” encompasses USDA employees, appointees, contractors, partners, interns, fellows, affiliates, and volunteers;
Federal data in any medium or form that the USDA or those on behalf of the USDA generates, collects, provides, transmits, stores, maintains, or accesses;
policy_statements.target: Federal data in any medium or form that the USDA or those on behalf of the USDA generates, collects, provides, transmits, stores, maintains, or accesses
conditions: that the USDA or those on behalf of the USDA generates, collects, provides, transmits, stores, maintains, or accesses

policy_statements.source_text: Systems or services, including cloud-based, that the USDA or those on behalf of the USDA use or operate.
policy_statements.target: Systems or services, including cloud-based, that the USDA or those on behalf of the USDA use or operate
conditions: that the USDA or those on behalf of the USDA use or operate

policy_statements.source_text: These include connections between or among data systems or services; and
Facilities from which USDA systems operate, whether the USDA or another entity on behalf of the USDA uses or operates them.
policy_statements.target: Facilities from which USDA systems operate
conditions: whether the USDA or another entity on behalf of the USDA uses or operates them

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this policy alters the need to protect national security systems or data.
This DR supersedes DR 3575-002, System and Information Integrity, dated August 16, 2018, in its entirety.
cross_references: DR 3575-002, System and Information Integrity, dated August 16, 2018

policy_statements.source_text: This DR takes effect immediately when published.
It remains in effect until superseded or expired.
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their SII procedures with this DR within 6 months of its publication.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This DR complies with:
Committee on National Security Systems policies, directives, and instructions;
The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014, 44 U.S.C. § 3551, et seq.;
cross_references: Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014, 44 U.S.C. § 3551, et seq

policy_statements.source_text: Federal requirements to set, implement, and enforce system integrity standards;
Intelligence community policies, directives, and instructions;

National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems;
cross_references: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: NIST FIPS PUB 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems;
cross_references: NIST FIPS PUB 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: NIST, Special Publication (SP) 800-37, Revision 2, Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and Organizations;
cross_references: NIST, Special Publication (SP) 800-37, Revision 2, Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: NIST, SP 800-39, Managing Information Security Risk: Organization, Mission, and Information System View;
cross_references: NIST, SP 800-39, Managing Information Security Risk: Organization, Mission, and Information System View

policy_statements.source_text: NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations; and
cross_references: NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB), A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource

policy_statements.source_text: SII refers to ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data systems and data.
It involves managing risks from system flaws and vulnerabilities, malicious code, unauthorized code changes, and inadequate error handling.
The goal is to provide assurance that someone has not tampered with or damaged the accessed data.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will set, implement, and maintain policies and procedures that include robust integration of SII throughout life cycle activities of all USDA data systems and services.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: policies and procedures that include robust integration of SII throughout life cycle activities of all USDA data systems and services

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will:
Identify, report, and correct system flaws;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Before installing, test software and firmware updates for efficacy and potential side effects;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Install security-relevant software and firmware updates according to the system security plan (SSP);
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Document security-relevant changes in the associated SSP;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Implement signature-based and non-signature-based detection mechanisms at system entry and exit points (e.g., servers, mobile devices, laptops);
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Update protection mechanisms when new releases become available;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Configure malicious code protection mechanisms to:
Perform periodic scans of the system weekly;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Scan files in real-time from endpoint and network entry and exit points as they are downloaded, opened, or executed;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: as they are downloaded, opened, or executed

policy_statements.source_text: Block and quarantine malicious activity; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Send alerts to authorized personnel only.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Address false positives during malicious code detection and the potential impact on the availability of the system;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: false positives during malicious code detection and the potential impact on the availability of the system

policy_statements.source_text: Configure systems to run anti-spam and anti-phishing detection solutions at system entry and exit points.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This will minimize false positives and false negatives;
Check for valid syntax and semantics (e.g., character set, length, numerical range, and acceptable values) of the system.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Verify inputs match specified definitions for format and content;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Configure systems to generate and send error messages to authorized personnel only; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Run Data Execution Prevention (DEP) to protect memory from unauthorized code execution.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: For system monitoring activities, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will work with the Cybersecurity and Privacy Operations Center (CPOC) to:
Comply with applicable federal laws, E.O.s, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: applicable federal laws, E.O.s, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines

policy_statements.source_text: Employ automated monitoring tools and layered protection mechanisms;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: automated monitoring tools and layered protection mechanisms

policy_statements.source_text: Continuously monitor all network traffic, as well as determined defined encrypted traffic;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: all network traffic, as well as determined defined encrypted traffic

policy_statements.source_text: Analyze outbound traffic at interior points (subnetworks and subsystems) and external interfaces to detect covert data exfiltration and anomalies;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure authorized personnel have access to monitoring information;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Identify network services that have not been authorized or approved and alert security personnel when detected; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: network services that have not been authorized or approved
conditions: that have not been authorized or approved

policy_statements.source_text: Employ an automated alert mechanism.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This will alert malicious, risky, or atypical activity to authorized personnel.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will work with the CPOC Security Operations Center to continuously monitor all systems within their purview for:
Attacks, or indicators of potential attacks;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Unauthorized local, network, and remote connections;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Unauthorized access, use, or downloads; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Attempts to deny service or degrade the performance.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will:
Only accept security alerts, advisories, and directives from the USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO);
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Generate internal security alerts, advisories, and directives as necessary;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: internal security alerts, advisories, and directives

policy_statements.source_text: Disseminate security alerts, advisories, and directives to personnel within their purview with a need to know, or those who implement the directives; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within their purview with a need to know, or those who implement the directives

policy_statements.source_text: Follow all alert, advisory, and directive implementation timelines according to the relative USDA cybersecurity directive.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: all alert, advisory, and directive implementation timelines

policy_statements.source_text: Refer to the following policies related to system integrity:
DR 3080-001, Records Management for guidance on data retention and management;
cross_references: DR 3080-001, Records Management

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems for guidance on privileged users and managing access to data systems;
cross_references: DR 3505-003, Access Control for Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3505-005, Cybersecurity Incident Management for incident management;
cross_references: DR 3505-005, Cybersecurity Incident Management

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information for guidance on personally identifiable information (PII) management;
cross_references: DR 3515-002, Privacy Policy and Compliance for Personally Identifiable Information

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3520-002, Configuration Management for guidance on system settings and configurations;
cross_references: DR 3520-002, Configuration Management

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3530-006, Scanning and Remediation of Configuration and Patch Vulnerabilities for guidance on system vulnerability management; and
cross_references: DR 3530-006, Scanning and Remediation of Configuration and Patch Vulnerabilities

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3575-003, Information Systems Log Retention Requirements for guidance on creating, storing, and maintaining various system logs.
cross_references: DR 3575-003, Information Systems Log Retention Requirements

policy_statements.source_text: The Cybersecurity Defense Operations Division (CDOD), Cybersecurity Watch Branch (CWB) will investigate malicious activity per DR 3505-005, Cybersecurity Incident Management.
policy_statements.actor_name: Cybersecurity Defense Operations Division (CDOD), Cybersecurity Watch Branch (CWB)
cross_references: DR 3505-005, Cybersecurity Incident Management

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Ensure compliance with all SII-related federal guidance;
Ensure USDA agencies have adequate resources to carry out SII requirements;
Serve as the Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP) during system authorizations, oversee privacy assessment conduct, and privacy and security control implementation; and
Report at least annually on the efficacy of deployed privacy and security program controls to all oversight bodies, as required.
policy_statements.target: efficacy of deployed privacy and security program controls

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CISO will:
Ensure SII control integrates with system life cycle management and all applicable processes;
Ensure that the Department and USDA agencies develop, maintain, and comply with federal and departmental SII requirements; and
Disseminate SII requirements and guidance to Mission Area Assistant CIOs, CISOs, and Information System Security Managers (ISSM).
Mission Area Assistant CIOs will:
Ensure personnel under their purview comply with all federal and departmental SII requirements;
Ensure relevant personnel assess, document, implement, and manage IT security risks; and
Serve as authorizing official for their Mission Area.
Ensure all data systems, applications, or common control sets in their purview have a current authorization to operate.
policy_statements.target: all data systems, applications, or common control sets in their purview

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CISOs will:
Coordinate with the USDA CISO to ensure SII controls integrate with system life cycle management, and all applicable processes;
Conduct a full assessment of implemented controls and enhancements to determine effectiveness;
Approve rules for acceptable data usage, creation, storage, processing, sharing, and protection for which they have statutory, management, or operational authority;
policy_statements.target: rules for acceptable data usage, creation, storage, processing, sharing, and protection for which they have statutory, management, or operational authority
conditions: for which they have statutory, management, or operational authority

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the principal data security specialist to all personnel in their purview;
Make sure their personnel promptly respond to security alerts; and

Ensure all personnel in their purview take annual information security awareness training per DR 3545-001, Information Security Awareness Program, and they complete role-based training as appropriate.
cross_references: DR 3545-001, Information Security Awareness Program

policy_statements.source_text: Agency Contracting Officers will:
Ensure contract documents define the performance expectations for each required SII security control as follows:
Describe measurable outcomes; and
Identify remedies.
Provide response requirements for any identified compliance failure with departmental SII requirements.
conditions: for any identified compliance failure with departmental SII requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area ISSMs will:
Ensure the personnel in their purview with SII responsibilities have awareness of and understand federal and departmental requirements;
policy_statements.target: personnel in their purview with SII responsibilities
conditions: in their purview with SII responsibilities

policy_statements.source_text: Verify systems under their purview have appropriately addressed SII controls;
Make sure their personnel immediately report incidents to CWB and respond to CDOD inquiries and communications regarding incidents;
Inform the Mission Area, agency, and staff office head, Mission Area Assistant CIO, and the USDA CIO of significant incidents;
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office head, Mission Area Assistant CIO, and the USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with System Owners to establish roles, privileges, access levels, and required controls to protect system data that is generated, used, stored, transmitted, and processed; and
Coordinate with, and offer guidance to, USDA personnel on managing life cycle activities and data security.
System Owners will:
Comply with, implement, and follow policy and procedures for SII;
Coordinate with ISSM and Information System Security Officers (ISSO) in other duties assigned under other USDA directives and federal guidance;
policy_statements.target: ISSM and Information System Security Officers (ISSO)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure vulnerability remediation processes integrate with configuration management processes;
Implement malicious code protection mechanisms;
Ensure mail and messaging systems deploy integrity protection mechanisms;
Ensure automatic protections respond appropriately to integrity violations;
Approve and monitor all maintenance activities;
Check their systems’ inputs for valid system inputs; and
Ensure that users, including information system support staff, are trained prior to gaining access to the data system.
policy_statements.target: users, including information system support staff

SII refers to ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data systems and data.
It involves managing risks from system flaws and vulnerabilities, malicious code, unauthorized code changes, and inadequate error handling.
The goal is to provide assurance that someone has not tampered with or damaged the accessed data.

Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will set, implement, and maintain policies and procedures that include robust integration of SII throughout life cycle activities of all USDA data systems and services.
